stem: $PQRS$ is a parallelogram, with its vertices named in order round it. $O$ is a point on the side $PQ$ such that $PS=OS$ and $QO=QR$. $S\hat{O}R={=s}^{\circ}$ and $Q\hat{O}R=x^{\circ}$. Calculate the value of $x$.
solution: Since $QO=QR$, $\triangle QOR$ is isosceles, so $Q\hat{R}O=Q\hat{O}R=x^{\circ}$ ($\angle$s opp equal sides).
$P$, $O$ and $Q$ lie on a straight line, so $S\hat{O}P+S\hat{O}R+Q\hat{O}R=180^{\circ}$ (sum of $\angle$s on a str line): $(2x)^{\circ}+{=s}^{\circ}+x^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$.
notes: Standard: the book's ex7-3-1c (page 254) with its numbers made into a parameter. The given angle SOR is s = 180 - 3t and the answer is the angle QOR = t, found by the book's route (QOR = QRO, so Q = 180 - 2x, so P = 2x by co-interior angles, SOP = P, angles on a straight line). The book leaves the step P = 2x unexplained; the worked solution here gives the co-interior-angles reason. The book diagram is replaced by wording (O on side PQ, vertices in order). Geometry verified by coordinates for t = 12, 20, 28, 30, 38. t = 28 is excluded only so no instance is the printed question verbatim.
